data.why: The repo ships a complete synthetic example (100 units, 2.79M spikes, 180 trials across 3 experiments) with pre-computed activity_summary.csv, exactly matching what the dashboard expects, so no data needs to be fabricated.

goals: Load spike-sorted units and trial timing, then compute each unit's baseline vs. stimulus-evoked firing rate
Inspect raster plots per unit per experiment to judge whether a unit responds to the stimulus
Set activity thresholds (baseline rate, response rate, rate difference, p-value) and see how many units pass live
Restrict which experiments are used for filtering vs. which are only shown in the summary table
Save and reload a reusable set of filter thresholds (filter_rules.csv) across sessions
Export the final list of filtered/active unit IDs to CSV for downstream analysis

review.summary: A well-built, accurately labelled tree that captures the dashboard's purpose (setting activity-based inclusion rules, checking units in rasters, saving rules and exporting the passing units), and all nine screens I opened back up their nodes. It needs light fixes before filing: add the missing setup/compute stage as an unreachable phase, move two edge-case probes out of the load-rules task, and merge the thin zoom feature into the raster feature.
